title: Active and passive voice
keyIdea: In the active voice the doer is the subject: Sam broke the window. In the passive voice the receiver of the action becomes the subject, and the verb is a form of be plus the past participle: The window was broken (by Sam). The doer can move into a by-phrase or be left out. Writers choose the passive to put the focus on the action or the thing it happened to, or when the doer is unknown or does not matter.

kid: Most sentences have a doer and a receiver. In Sam broke the window, Sam does the breaking. The window gets broken. Sam comes first, so the sentence is active.
We can flip it. The window was broken by Sam. Now the window comes first. The verb changes to was broken. That is the passive voice.
To make the passive, use a form of be, like is, are, was or were. Add the past participle, like broken, made or written. The doer can go after by, or it can go.
Use active when you want clear, lively writing. Use passive when the action matters more than who did it. It also helps when you do not know who did it: My bike was stolen.
adult: In England, Year 6 pupils learn to use passive verbs to change how a sentence presents information. They learn the terms active and passive. The curriculum's own example is I broke the window in the greenhouse versus The window in the greenhouse was broken (by me).

To form the passive, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject. The verb becomes a form of be plus the past participle. Be must agree with the new subject: The meals are cooked by the chef. The doer is called the agent. It moves into an optional by-phrase. A passive without one, such as The match was cancelled, is an agentless passive.

Common mistakes: using the simple past instead of the participle (was broke, was blew). Thinking any sentence with was is passive, so The cake was delicious or Tom was running get called passive. Thinking the first noun must be the doer. Believing the passive is always more formal or better. Be careful with get passives such as got stolen: they are passive too, but informal.

In the lab, learners find the doer in active and passive sentences. They build passives from chunks and avoid a wrong participle or a wrong form of be. They sort real passives from look-alikes and decide when to keep or cut the by-phrase. Last, they choose the voice that fits a science method, a story and a news report.

familyTip: Read a news headline together, such as Road closed after crash. Ask: what happened, and do we know who did it? Then say it both ways, active and passive, and talk about which one the reporter needed.

visual.caption: Active or passive? Drag each card to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: The race was won by Priya.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: find the doer, flip sentences into the passive, spot look-alikes, keep or cut the by-phrase, then choose a voice for a purpose.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
choices: The letter was posted by Kai.
Kai posted the letter.
Kai was posting the letter.
practice.hint: Look for the receiver as subject, then a form of be plus a past participle.
practice.explain: The letter was posted by Kai is passive: the letter is the subject and was posted is be + past participle. Kai was posting is active, because Kai is still the doer.

practice.prompt: A science method has {a} passive sentences and {b} active sentences. How many sentences use be + a past participle with the receiver as subject?
practice.hint: Only passive sentences have the receiver as subject with be + past participle.
practice.explain: Only the {a} passive sentences do. The {b} active sentences keep the doer as subject.

practice.prompt: Make it passive: The children painted the fence.
choices: The fence was painted by the children.
The fence painted the children.
The fence were painted by the children.
practice.hint: Fence is one thing, so which form of be agrees with it?
practice.explain: The fence becomes the subject, so it takes was, and painted stays as the past participle. Swapping the nouns changes the meaning.

practice.prompt: Zara rewrites {n} active sentences as passives and cuts the by-phrase from {k} of them. How many of her passives still name the doer?
practice.hint: Each passive starts with a by-phrase. Take away the ones she cut.
practice.explain: {n} passives minus {k} cut by-phrases leaves {=n-k} that still name the doer. The rest are agentless passives.

pool.prompt: In The bridge was built by Romans, who did the building?
choices: the Romans
the bridge
We are not told
pool.hint: In the passive, the doer comes after the word by.
pool.explain: The Romans are the agent. The bridge is the subject but it is the receiver of the building.

choices: We were tired.
We were chosen.
We were chosen by the coach.
pool.hint: Is the word after were a past participle, or a describing word?
pool.explain: Tired here describes how we felt, so We were tired is not a passive. Were chosen is be + past participle.

pool.prompt: Pick the correct passive: The storm ___ the roof off.
choices: The roof was blown off by the storm.
The roof was blew off by the storm.
The roof blown off by the storm.
pool.hint: You need a form of be and the past participle of blow.
pool.explain: Blow, blew, blown: blown is the past participle, and was is the form of be.

pool.prompt: Why does a lab report write The mixture was filtered?
choices: The process matters more than who did it
The passive is always better writing
It hides a mistake
pool.hint: Who would need to repeat the method, and what do they need to know?
pool.explain: A method needs the steps, not the name of the person, so the passive keeps the focus on the process.

pool.prompt: Which sentence is an agentless passive?
choices: The shop was closed early.
The shop was closed by the owner.
The owner closed the shop.
pool.hint: Agentless means no by-phrase naming the doer.
pool.explain: The shop was closed early is passive with no by-phrase, so the doer is not named.

pool.prompt: Which version suits an adventure story best?
choices: The knight drew his sword and charged.
The sword was drawn by the knight.
A charge was made.
pool.hint: Stories feel fast when the doer leads the sentence.
pool.explain: Active voice puts the knight first, doing things, which keeps the action lively.

pool.prompt: A news report has {a} passive sentences. {b} of them name the doer with by. How many are agentless?
pool.hint: Agentless passives are the ones without a by-phrase.
pool.explain: {a} passives minus {b} with a by-phrase leaves {=a-b} agentless passives.

pool.prompt: Make it passive: The judges choose the winners.
choices: The winners are chosen by the judges.
The winners is chosen by the judges.
The winners chose the judges.
pool.hint: Winners is plural. Which present form of be agrees with it?
pool.explain: Are agrees with winners, and chosen is the past participle of choose.

pool.prompt: A report has {a} sentences. {b} of them are passive. How many are in the active voice?
pool.hint: Every sentence with a verb is either active or passive. Take away the passives.
pool.explain: {a} sentences minus {b} passives leaves {=a-b} active sentences.
